data.narrative:
Blackstar is a Seed-stage AI & Software company founded by Daniel Edrisian, former OpenAI Codex engineer whose prior startup (Alex, YC W24) was acqui-hired by OpenAI in September 2025. The company has raised $12M to date. The comparable universe consists of 9 private AI & Software companies (including Figure AI, Scale AI, Reflection AI, and Applied Intuition) and 1 public peer (Palantir).

Given the early stage and nascent peer set, only one valuation method is reliably applicable. Stage-progression analysis, using the $12M total raised as a base proxy and applying a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical for Seed-to-next-stage progression, yields $30M. A peer-median approach is not supportable; while 12 same-sector peers exist, zero same-stage comparables, only one adjacent-stage comparable, and zero similar-tier comparables are available—insufficient density to anchor a robust median without introducing material bias.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $26M to $34M, with a median of $30M. This range reflects stage-appropriate progression from deployed capital. Key uncertainties include the absence of tight peer comparables at identical stage and valuation tier, limiting the ability to cross-check the step-up multiple against market precedent. Near-term revenue traction, product-market fit metrics, and the trajectory of the competitive AI coding-assistant landscape will be material to any upward or downward revision.
